title: Low-depth simulation of non-Markovianity under quantum hardware noise
summary: Simulating open quantum systems on digital quantum computers typically relies on the use of auxiliary qubits, resulting in overheads of noisy multi-qubit gates, that severely limit execution on near-term hardware. In this work, we explore the simulation of non-Markovian dynamics as well as memory channels leveraging the method of trajectory mixing, valid for mixed unitary channels. This allows to drastically reduce circuit depth, trading entangling gates for a statistical mixture of independent, pure state trajectories.
